welcome.title: Welcome to Home Budget
welcome.body: Your household money in one place: what came in, what went out, what is left this month and what is coming. Here is where everything lives.

overview.title: $t(nav.overview)
overview.body: Start here every time: this month's income, expenses, what is left to spend and the bills coming up.

transactions.title: $t(nav.transactions)
transactions.body: Every income, expense and transfer from all accounts. Add one with Ctrl+N, filter by month, account or category, and sort out what still needs a category.

budget.title: $t(nav.budget)
budget.body: An amount per category for each month: what is left to budget, what is left to spend, and where you went over the plan.

accounts.title: $t(nav.accounts)
accounts.body: Bank accounts, cards and cash with their balances. Quick setup creates the usual ones in a minute.

recurring.title: $t(nav.recurring)
recurring.body: Rent, utilities, insurance and subscriptions: what is due soon, what is paid, and what fixed costs take each month.

debts.title: $t(nav.debts)
debts.body: Loans, card instalments and money owed: what is left to pay, when it ends, and how much sooner it ends with a bit extra each month.

insight.title: $t(nav.projections) · $t(nav.reports)
insight.body: Coming soon: where the balance is heading, and where the money went by category, member and month.

member.title: Who is using the app
member.body: Shows which parent is at the computer. What you enter is recorded under their name; click to switch.

settings.title: $t(nav.settings)
settings.body: Theme, language, date format and the data folder. You can replay this tour from here.

search.title: Find anything
search.body: Press Ctrl+K to jump to any page or run a command, such as switching theme or printing a budget worksheet.

notifications.title: $t(notifications.title)
notifications.body: Bills due or late, income that has not come in, categories over budget and rows to categorise. Act on each from here; the red number counts the new ones.

portable.badge_hint: Portable edition: data is kept next to the app, on this drive
portable.data_hint: Everything is saved next to the app, so it travels with the drive. A copy is kept in backups/ each time the app starts.

worksheet.button_hint: A blank monthly budget sheet to plan on paper (PDF)
worksheet.title: Budget · {{month}}
worksheet.subtitle: Monthly budget worksheet · printed {{date}}
worksheet.footnote: Write the planned amount at the start of the month and the actual amount at the end. Difference = planned − actual: a negative number means you spent more than planned. Use the empty rows for your own categories.
worksheet.statement_footnote: Planned = the month's amount plus anything carried over from last month. Difference = planned − actual: a negative number means more was spent than planned (or more income came in than expected).
worksheet.year_footnote: Planned amount per month; blank = nothing planned. The Actual line under each group shows what came in or went out in the months so far.

pdf.preview_hint: This is what the PDF will look like.

error.UNKNOWN: Something went wrong. Please try again.
error.INVALID_REPORT: The report could not be created.
error.PDF_EXPORT_FAILED: The PDF could not be saved there. Choose another folder or close the file if it is open in another program.
error.OPEN_FILE_FAILED: The file could not be opened. Open it from its folder instead.
error.OPEN_DATA_DIR_FAILED: The data folder could not be opened.
error.INVALID_INPUT: Some details are missing or not valid. Check the form and try again.
error.ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND: That account no longer exists or is archived.
error.CATEGORY_EXISTS: A category with this name already exists here.
error.TRANSACTION_IS_TRANSFER: This is a transfer; edit it as a transfer.
error.SAME_ACCOUNT: A transfer needs two different accounts.
error.TRANSFER_IMPORTED: A side that came from a bank statement stays in its account.
error.TRANSFER_MISMATCH: These two rows can't form a transfer: they need opposite amounts in different accounts.
error.VOUCHER_NO_TRANSFER_OUT: Money on a meal-voucher card can only be spent, not moved to another account.
error.HOLDER_REQUIRED: Choose which parent the meal-voucher card belongs to.
error.IMPORT_FILE_UNREADABLE: The file could not be read. Check that it still exists and is not open in another program.
error.IMPORT_FILE_TOO_LARGE: This file is too large to be a bank statement. Choose the statement export of one account.
error.IMPORT_PREVIEW_EXPIRED: The preview is out of date. Read the file again.
error.MEMBER_NOT_FOUND: That parent no longer exists or is archived.
error.MEMBER_NAME_TAKEN: There is already a parent with this name.
error.CARD_DUPLICATE: Two cards have the same last 4 digits.
error.CARD_NOT_FOUND: A card no longer exists. Close and reopen the account.
error.CATEGORY_IN_USE: Still in use: move or merge what uses it first.
error.BUDGET_SOURCE_EMPTY: Last month has nothing to copy.
error.INSTITUTION_NOT_FOUND: That bank no longer exists or is archived.
error.INSTITUTION_NAME_TAKEN: There is already a bank with this name.
error.INSTITUTION_IN_USE: Accounts use this bank, so its type can't change.
error.TRANSACTION_ALREADY_LINKED: That row already pays another due date.
error.DEBT_OWNED_RULE: These are a debt's instalments. Change them on the Debts & loans page.
error.PAYMENT_ALREADY_LINKED: That row already counts for a debt.
error.INSTALMENT_TOO_LOW: This instalment never pays it off: it does not cover the monthly interest.
error.CSV_EXPORT_FAILED: The CSV could not be saved there. Choose another folder or close the file if it is open in Excel.

categories.quick_subtitle: It is chosen for this row straight away.
categories.title: Categories
categories.intro: Groups decide how rows count in totals; categories are what you sort rows into.
categories.empty: No groups yet. Add one to start sorting.
categories.delete_group_blocked: Has categories: move, merge or archive them first
categories.group_empty: No categories in this group yet.
categories.delete_blocked: Has transactions: merge or archive it instead
categories.group_type_hint: Decides where its rows show in totals and the budget.
categories.move_type_change_one: Its {{count}} transaction will count as {{to}} instead of {{from}}.
categories.move_type_change_other: Its {{count}} transactions will count as {{to}} instead of {{from}}.
categories.merge_instead: Merge into the existing one instead
categories.merge_explain: Every transaction and rule of {{name}} moves to the category you choose; {{name}} is then archived.
categories.archived_notice: {{name}} archived. Its transactions keep their category and still count in totals.
categories.archive_group_message: The group and its categories disappear from the pickers. Their transactions keep their category and still count in totals. You can restore them under Archived.
categories.archive_message: It disappears from the pickers. Its transactions keep it and still count in totals. You can restore it under Archived.
categories.delete_message: Nothing uses it; {{rules}} go with it. This can’t be undone.

entry.title: Add transaction
entry.kind_locked: A transfer stays a transfer. Delete it and add a new entry to change this.
entry.add_and_new_hint: Saves and keeps the form open with the same date and account (Ctrl+Enter)
entry.delete_message: It is removed from the log and the account balance changes. This cannot be undone.
entry.delete_transfer_message: Both sides of the transfer are removed, unless a side came from a bank statement. This cannot be undone.

amount_hint.EXPENSE: Type it without a minus: it is recorded as money going out.
amount_hint.TRANSFER: Moves between your own accounts; never counted as income or expense.

entry.payee_hint: Shop or person. A payee you used before brings back its category.
entry.differs_from_statement: This row came from a bank statement. A different amount or date will no longer match the statement.

errors.amount_invalid: Enter an amount above zero, e.g. 12,50.
errors.same_account: Choose a different account from the one the money leaves.
errors.category_required: Choose a category, so totals stay right.

entry.for_hint: Who it was for; “Household” when it is for the whole home.

log.title: Transactions
log.uncategorised_banner_one: {{count}} transaction has no category, so totals are incomplete.
log.uncategorised_banner_other: {{count}} transactions have no category, so totals are incomplete.
log.all_sorted_body: No transaction is waiting to be categorised.
log.no_match_body: Try another account, type or category, or clear the filters.
log.empty_body: Add an expense, income or transfer with Add transaction ({{keys}}).
log.no_accounts_body: Every transaction belongs to an account: a bank account, a card or cash. Quick setup creates the usual ones in a minute.
log.transfer_hint: Between your own accounts; not counted as income or expense
log.payee_clear_hint: Leave empty to clear it; imported rows then show the bank text again.
log.no_bank_text: Only rows with bank text can teach a rule
log.delete_many_message: They are removed from the log and the account balances change. This cannot be undone.

members.name: Name
members.name_hint: As it should appear on transactions, e.g. “Andreas”.
members.colour_hint: Tells parents apart in lists, always next to the name.
members.empty: Add both parents: every transaction then records who entered it and who it was for.
members.this_pc_hint: Whatever is entered on this PC is recorded under this name.
members.archive_message: They no longer appear in pickers. Their transactions keep the name, and you can restore them.
members.who_is_using_hint: Pick who you are; what you enter is recorded under your name.
members.using_hint: New entries are recorded as entered by {{name}}. Click to switch.

banks.name: Name
banks.name_hint: As it should appear on your accounts, e.g. “Revolut”.
banks.kind_hint: A meal-card issuer (like Edenred) is offered only for meal-voucher cards.
banks.kind_locked: Accounts use it, so its type stays as it is.
banks.empty: No banks yet. Add the banks where you keep accounts.
banks.archive_message: It is no longer offered for new accounts. Accounts already at it keep it, and you can restore it.

accounts.food_only_hint: Spendable only on food; not counted in the total of your accounts.
accounts.voucher_negative_hint: More was spent than the card holds. Check the opening balance or add the missing top-up.
accounts.name: Name
accounts.new_bank_hint: As it should appear on your accounts, e.g. “Revolut”.
accounts.opening_balance_hint: What the account held on the opening date.
accounts.opening_balance_card_hint: What you owed on the card, as a negative amount (e.g. -350,00).
accounts.opening_balance_voucher_hint: The balance shown in the Edenred or Up Hellas app today.
accounts.opening_date_hint: Transactions are counted from this day.
accounts.archive_message: It disappears from lists and pickers. Its transactions stay and still count in past totals. You can restore it later.
accounts.no_match_body: Change or clear the filters to see your accounts again.

errors.card_last4: Type exactly 4 digits, as on the card.
errors.card_duplicate: This card is already in the list.

accounts.quick_intro: The household's usual accounts, ready to go. Untick what you don't have, rename if you like, and type today's balance. Meal-voucher cards (Edenred, Up Hellas) can be added afterwards with Add account.
accounts.quick_cash_question: How much cash do you have now?
accounts.quick_hint: Cards: type what you owe as a negative amount. Leave a balance empty for zero.
accounts.quick_fix: Check the highlighted rows: each needs a name and a valid amount.
accounts.holder_hint: Whose account it is; “Joint” when it belongs to both.
accounts.holder_hint_voucher: The parent whose employer loads the card.
accounts.cards_hint_credit: Main and supplementary cards, by their last 4 digits.
accounts.cards_hint_debit: Debit cards on this account, by their last 4 digits.

rules.saved: Rule saved. Next time it is sorted for you.
rules.saved_more_one: Rule saved, and {{count}} more row sorted.
rules.saved_more_other: Rule saved, and {{count}} more rows sorted.
rules.intro: Rules sort imported rows by their bank text. A rule you teach beats the starter list.
rules.pattern_required: Type the text the bank prints, e.g. the shop’s name.
rules.pattern_stored: Matched as “{{pattern}}”: no accents, Greek and Latin spellings alike.
rules.pattern_hint: As the statement prints it, e.g. ΣΚΛΑΒΕΝΙΤΗΣ.
rules.payee_hint: Optional: shown instead of the bank text.
rules.apply_now: Also sort the rows still waiting for a category that match it
rules.empty: No rules yet. They are learned when you sort an imported row (“Always put X in Y?”).
rules.added_notice_zero: Rule added. Next imports are sorted with it.
rules.added_notice_one: Rule added, and {{count}} waiting row sorted.
rules.added_notice_other: Rule added, and {{count}} waiting rows sorted.
rules.saved_notice: Rule saved. Next imports are sorted with it.
rules.delete_message: Rows keep their category; only future imports change.
rules.tester_title: Which rule catches a bank text?
rules.tester_hint: Paste the text as it appears on your statement to see where an import will put it.
rules.tester_none: No rule catches this text; it will wait for a category.
rules.already_caught_starter: The starter rule «{{pattern}}» → {{category}} catches this text today; your rule will take over.
rules.already_caught_yours: Your rule «{{pattern}}» → {{category}} already catches this text. Change that rule instead, or make this one more specific.
rules.prompt_many: Always put {{merchants}} in {{category}}? One rule each.
rules.saved_many_sorted_one: {{rules}} rules saved, and {{count}} more row sorted.
rules.saved_many_sorted_other: {{rules}} rules saved, and {{count}} more rows sorted.

import.title: Import a bank statement
import.choose_hint: Use the CSV or Excel export from your e-banking. The file is read on this computer and never sent anywhere.
import.no_accounts: Add a bank account or card first; cash has no statement.
import.no_rows: No transactions were found in this file. Choose the statement export (CSV or Excel) for one account.
import.profile_saved: Read with this account’s saved columns
import.same_file: This file was imported on {{date}} ({{count}} rows). Rows already in the app are left out.
import.target_link: Same as the row I entered
import.why_invalid_DATE: Line {{line}}: the date could not be read
import.why_invalid_AMOUNT: Line {{line}}: the amount could not be read
import.why_invalid_CURRENCY: Line {{line}}: in another currency than the account
import.why_duplicate: You entered {{payee}} on {{date}}. Tick to keep one row.
import.why_atm: Cash taken out: moves to {{account}}, not an expense
import.why_card_payment: Card payment: pairs with the card statement when you import it
import.map_intro: This file’s columns are not known yet. Say once which column is which; the account remembers it for the next statement.
import.map_header_row_hint: Click a row above or pick it here.
import.map_mode_columns: Money out and money in columns
import.map_invert: Purchases are positive numbers in this file
import.map_invert_hint: Usual for card statements: they are turned into money out.
import.map_no_match: These columns did not give any transactions. Check the date and amount columns.
import.showing_one: Showing the rows of one import.
import.undo_message_one: The {{count}} imported row is removed and balances go back. Rows you entered by hand stay. You can import the file again later.
import.undo_message_other: The {{count}} imported rows are removed and balances go back. Rows you entered by hand stay. You can import the file again later.
import.balance_explain: On {{date}} the bank says {{bank}} but the app shows {{app}}: a difference of {{amount}}.
import.balance_hint: Check the account’s opening balance, rows entered by hand, or an earlier statement not imported yet.

subscriptions.hints_subtitle: The same merchant, about the same amount, every month or year.
subscriptions.sorted: {{name}} now goes to {{category}}, this time and next.

budget.title: Budget
budget.tile_income_future: What you expect to come in this month
budget.ltb_positive: Income not given a job yet
budget.ltb_negative: The plan is more than the expected income
budget.lts_future: What the plan allows for spending
budget.carry_hint: Unspent money carries into next month
budget.action_carry_on: Carry unspent money into next month
budget.empty_body: Give each category an amount: income first, then bills and spending. Copying fills only the empty lines.
budget.copy_nothing: Every line already had an amount; nothing changed.
budget.fill_plan: Fill empty lines from the plan of {{month}}
budget.clear_message: Every planned amount of this month is removed. Transactions are not touched.
budget.banner_uncategorised_one: {{count}} transaction this month has no category, so it is not in the budget.
budget.banner_uncategorised_other: {{count}} transactions this month have no category, so they are not in the budget.
budget.banner_unplanned_one: {{amount}} was spent in {{count}} category with no plan.
budget.banner_unplanned_other: {{amount}} was spent in {{count}} categories with no plan.
budget.no_categories_body: The budget gives each category an amount. Add categories first.
budget.no_rules: No bills yet: add them in Subscriptions & bills
budget.rules_nothing: Every line with a bill already had an amount; nothing changed.
budget.year_income_future: What you expect to come in this year
budget.year_lts_future: What the year's plan allows for spending
budget.year_carried_in: {{amount}} carried in from the month before
budget.year_fill_row_none: Nothing planned this year and no bills to start from
budget.year_fill_plan: Fill empty months from the plan of {{month}}
budget.year_fill_plan_none: Fill empty months from a month's plan
budget.year_no_plan_yet: No month has a plan yet
budget.year_fill_nothing: Every month already had an amount; nothing changed.
budget.year_empty_body: Lay out the whole year at once. Filling writes only empty months, from {{from}} to December; you can change any month afterwards.
budget.year_copy_plan: Fill the year from the plan of {{month}}
budget.year_compare_future: Nothing booked in a coming year yet
budget.year_compare_none: No transactions in {{year}} to compare with.

recurring.subtitle: What is due soon, what is paid, and what fixed costs take each month
recurring.from_hint: From a charge that repeats in your statements; check the date and amount.
recurring.name: Name
recurring.name_hint: As you call it: Netflix, Car insurance, Rent
recurring.amount_varies_hint: electricity, water: any amount counts as paid
recurring.anchor_hint: Later dates keep its day of the month
recurring.account_hint: Only rows of this account will match
recurring.provision: That is {{amount}} a month. The budget offers it as the plan for this category, so the money is there when the bill comes.
recurring.carry_over: Carry unspent money over in {{category}}, so the monthly amount builds up
recurring.match_hint: Rows whose text contains this mark the bill paid. Empty = the name.
recurring.match_count_one: Matches {{count}} row of the last year
recurring.match_count_other: Matches {{count}} rows of the last year

errors.interval_invalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to 99.
errors.ends_before_start: The last payment cannot be before the first.

recurring.no_row_hint: Paid some other way, or the row is not in the app
recurring.paid_in_cash: Paid in cash: add the row
recurring.cash_intro: A new row is added to the log with the bill's category.
recurring.hints_banner_one: {{count}} charge in your statements looks like a subscription.
recurring.hints_banner_other: {{count}} charges in your statements look like subscriptions.
recurring.empty_body: Add rent, utilities, insurance and subscriptions once. Rows from your bank mark them paid by themselves.
recurring.tile_monthly_hint_one: {{count}} bill, yearly ones spread over 12 months
recurring.tile_monthly_hint_other: {{count}} bills, yearly ones spread over 12 months
recurring.tile_overdue_hint: Not seen in your transactions yet
recurring.nothing_due_body: No payments are due until the end of next month.
recurring.track_hint: Add as a bill: due dates, paid marks and a monthly plan
recurring.budget_use_hint: Plan {{amount}} for {{name}}: the monthly cost of its bills
recurring.debt_rules_note_one: {{count}} debt's instalments are listed on the Debts & loans page.
recurring.debt_rules_note_other: {{count}} debts' instalments are listed on the Debts & loans page.

debts.subtitle: Loans, card instalments and money owed: what is left, when it ends, and what paying a bit more would do.
debts.empty_body: Add a loan, interest-free card instalments or money lent within the family. Its instalments show up with the bills and tick themselves off when the bank row comes in.

kind_hint.LOAN: A loan with a fixed monthly payment, with or without interest.
kind_hint.INSTALMENTS: A purchase split into interest-free monthly instalments on a credit card.
kind_hint.PERSONAL: Money borrowed from or lent to family and friends.

debts.no_cards: Add the credit card in Accounts first.
debts.already_paying: Already paying it? Enter what is left today and the instalments left.
debts.rate_hint: Leave empty for an interest-free loan.
debts.repays: Paid back in fixed monthly amounts
debts.repays_hint: the instalments then show up with the bills
debts.preview_empty: Fill in the amount and the term to see the instalment.
debts.pay_from_hint: The bank row from this account ticks each instalment off.
debts.category_hint: Where the instalments count in the budget.
debts.match_hint: Words of the bank text that mark an instalment. Empty = the name.

errors.amount_invalid: Enter an amount above zero, e.g. 1.500,00.
errors.months_invalid: Enter a number of months from 1 to 600.
errors.instalment_too_low: This instalment never pays it off: it does not even cover the monthly interest.

debts.never_ends: At this instalment the debt never ends: it does not cover the monthly interest. Check the rate or set the balance from the bank's statement.
debts.paid_off_banner: Paid off. Archive it to keep the page tidy; its history stays.
debts.paid_back_banner: All paid back. Archive it to keep the page tidy; its history stays.
debts.schedule_hint: Imported rows tick instalments off on their own
debts.tile_monthly_hint: what the debts take each month
debts.tile_free_never: one debt never ends at its instalment

balance.title: Balance of {{name}}
balance.intro: Enter the balance from the bank's statement (a variable rate or fees can make it differ). Payments after its date are taken off it.

payment.extra_intro: For money paid on top of the instalments; it comes straight off the balance. Instalments tick off on their own.
payment.cash_intro_out: Adds the payment to the log and counts it for this debt.
payment.cash_intro_in: Adds the money received to the log and counts it for this debt.

hint.AVALANCHE: Avalanche: the least interest in total.
hint.SNOWBALL: Snowball: quick wins, one debt gone sooner.

plan.better_one: {{count}} month sooner and {{interest}} less interest than the instalments alone.
plan.better_other: {{count}} months sooner and {{interest}} less interest than the instalments alone.
plan.as_is: At the instalments alone, with {{interest}} interest still to pay. Add an extra amount to see what it changes.
plan.never: A debt never ends at its instalment, so there is no debt-free date. Raise the extra amount.
plan.nothing: No debt with monthly instalments to plan. Add a loan or card instalments first.
plan.order_hint: The extra goes to the first; when it is paid off its instalment moves to the next

why.never_ends: The instalment does not cover the interest

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.clear_body: They come back only when something new needs a hand (a new due date, new rows to categorise).
notifications.empty_body: Bills due, late income, categories over budget and rows to categorise show up here.

to-categorise.detail_one: Give it a category so the budget adds up.
to-categorise.detail_other: Give them a category so the budget adds up.

toast.summary_body: Bills due today or late. Open Home Budget to see them.

settings.toasts_hint: While the app is open, a bill due today, an overdue one or late income pops up once.
settings.lead_hint: How early the bell shows a bill. A bill can have its own in its form (More).

rule.remind_hint: When the bell shows this one.

projections.title: Projections
projections.meta_repeated: other months repeat the plan of {{month}}
projections.no_accounts_body: The forecast starts from the money in your accounts. Add them first.
projections.chart_title: Balance at the end of each month
projections.chart_label: Balance from {{start}} today to {{end}}; lowest {{lowest}} in {{month}}. Use the arrow keys to read each month.
projections.tile_lowest_below: Below zero at the end of {{month}}
projections.banner_below: The balance goes below zero in {{month}} ({{amount}}). Lower that month's plan or move money in time.
projections.empty_banner: No budget plan or bills yet, so the balance stays flat. Add a plan or your bills to see where it is heading.
projections.footnote: Each month counts the larger of its budget plan and its bills per category; a month with no plan of its own repeats this month's plan. Planned savings stay in your accounts, so they are not taken off; transfers between your accounts change nothing.

reports.title: Reports
reports.empty_body: No transactions between {{period}}. Try a longer period.
reports.custom_backwards: The start date is after the end date.
reports.no_category_hint: categorise them to see where they belong
reports.trend_title_quarter: Income and spending per quarter (more than 24 months)
reports.trend_label: In {{in}}, out {{out}} over the period. Arrow keys read each month; Enter shows its transactions.
reports.balance_title: Money in accounts at each month end
reports.balance_vouchers: Meal vouchers, not in the total
reports.pdf_footnote: Transfers between your own accounts are left out. A refund lowers the category it belongs to.
